metadata.architecture: single-channel causal attention with an attention-dominant fixed residual mixture and tied readout
metadata.author: declarative architecture search
metadata.mechanism_hypothesis: An attention-dominant fixed mixture can preserve local token-position identity while retaining strong causal context, improving addition accuracy over a pure scalar-attention bottleneck without adding parameters.
metadata.name: Single-Channel Attention-Dominant Mix
metadata.research_alternative_explanation: Width-one attention discards essential local token and position information, so a small direct route is needed even when attention remains dominant.
metadata.research_challenged_assumption: Forcing every logit representation exclusively through scalar causal attention is better than retaining any token-position bypass.
metadata.research_current_explanation: The current direction assumes a residual bypass interferes with context selection and that direct attention should therefore improve aligned-digit and carry computation.
metadata.research_decision_rule: Retain the child only if it is valid, preserves the public eligibility floor, and improves public accuracy at the same trusted parameter count or reduces that count.
metadata.research_discriminating_evidence: A public gain over 0.000000 favors local-information preservation; no gain favors bypass interference or a more fundamental width-one capacity limit.
metadata.research_evidence: The direct-attention parent scored 0.000000 publicly, providing no evidence that eliminating the bypass improves addition computation.
metadata.research_expected_result: The 0.5-to-1.0 local-to-attention mixture should keep trusted parameter count unchanged while improving public accuracy if information loss caused the direct model's failure.
metadata.research_next_experiment: Mix the positioned embedding and causal-attention output with fixed weights 0.5 and 1.0 before the tied readout.
metadata.research_previous_interpretation: Removing the bypass yielded a 0.000000 public score, so the direct-attention bottleneck did not produce an observed improvement.
